newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended sharply higher on Tuesday after a late movement which pushed prices higher ahead of the U.S. Fed FOMC's rate decision later tonight.
Dealers said the positive tone of the Italian market supported bonos, but they did not hide their surprise.

"I was a bit surprised....maybe it was just one buyer. I have the same opinion I had before -- the Spanish market stands at very risky levels, and I feel more confident with three- to five year bonds than with ten-year," said Jose Ramon Arechederra chied trader at ABN Amro in Madrid.
The 10-year cash spread over Bunds fell to a fresh record low in the afternoon of 69 basis points, than ended at 71 basis points.
Earlier on Tuesday one strategist at the brokerage house Morgan Stanley in London told Reuters it was expecting the yield differential to fall to around 25 or 30 basis points by the end of this year.
On Wednesday the Spanish Treasury is expected to offer six-month bills, whose yield is seen falling from previous levels, dealers said.
